figures.window: **Rationale:** This is the score I moved on most, and rule 5 decided it. Anchor 2 asks that cross-boundary calls go through something identifiable as a port. W has three cross-boundary calls and they go through three different places: the write through _append_line (:119-121), the read straight to self._ledger_path.read_text() inside the public ledger_lines() query (:64), and construction straight to write_text('') (:42). Two of the three bypass the only seam, and one of those two is a query the feature lists as observable state -- so the rules and the filesystem are interleaved rather than separated, and there is no one thing I can point at and call the port. Anchor 2 is therefore not fully satisfied. Anchor 0's wording ('state is written from everywhere') is too harsh -- W's in-memory state has clean single writers, as D2 records -- and anchor 1's wording ('named ... and the code does not follow them') does not literally fit either, because W declares no boundary in prose at all. Torn between 1 and 2, rule 5 says take the lower and say why: I took the lower on the seam, and the deciding fact is the read path at :64. Recorded fairly: FEATURE.md:113-122 makes 'whether the durable side is reached through an interface, a callable, or directly' a free choice and asks a judge not to read a difference there as a defect. figures.near: one of two copies of a fact deleted, and it is the
figures.window: I diffed the two trees myself before reading either note. The whole delta is: `mutation_check.py` and `NOTES.md` byte-identical; `quota_ledger.py` loses one field and gains one derivation; `test_quota_ledger.py` gains one parametrised test and loses nothing. That is a five-line change, and the question is whether it is a simplification. WHAT GOT SIMPLER. The before tree kept `_held`, a per-tenant running total, at five sites (artifact_N/quota_ledger.py:62 init, :74 read, :111 reserve, :122 commit, :136 release). At every instant `_held[t]` equalled `sum(r.amount for r in _outstanding.values() if r.tenant == t)` -- a second representation of a number `_outstanding` already carried, maintained by hand at three write sites, with nothing in either suite asserting the two agreed. The after tree computes it once, where it is used (quota_ledger.py:70-76). This is not an edge deleted to move a metric (the D2 caveat's failure mode, and the first thing I checked for): it is one of two copies of a fact deleted, and it is the copy R1 is a rule ABOUT. I measured the consequence rather than asserting it -- I seeded three faults that can only exist in the before tree because the second copy exists (reserve crediting the hold to the wrong tenant; commit not decrementing; release not decrementing) and one that can only exist in the after tree because the derivation exists (the held sum dropping its tenant filter). Three fault sites became one. All four are caught by both suites, so this is fault SURFACE removed, not an uncaught hazard removed -- I am stating the weaker true thing. HOW THE BEHAVIOR SURVIVED IT. I did not take the artifact's word. I wrote my own differential and ran the two implementations side by side: 1500 walks x 60 operations, three tenants plus an unknown one, quotas 0-40 so ids run past r9, commit/release ids drawn r1..r30 so most miss, amounts -3..45, comparing every (status, reason, reservation_id), every observable, AND the exception type and message from every query on every tenant after every operation. Zero divergences. Both trees also pass the shared contract 28/28 and reproduce the twelve-mutant table identically -- I ran both. That is D4 >= 3 established independently, which is anchor 4's requirement. BEFORE AND AFTER FIGURES ARE BOTH RECORDED. In the artifact: REVISION-NOTES.md:8-21 records the pre-change run (28 passed, 37 passed, 11/12 caught) and the post-change run (28, 39, 11/12); :43-44 records the structural before/after (commit touched four things, now three); :129-131 records `_held` at 5 occurrences, all removed. On this card: instance_state 7 -> 6, code_lines 283 -> 280. DISAGREEMENT WITH THE MECHANICAL BLOCK, and it is the finding I would not want lost: the complexity descriptor does NOT unambiguously say this got simpler. branch_points goes UP, 26 -> 27, because the derivation adds a comprehension condition; callables, classes, modules, max_depth, max_branch_points_in_callable, public_surface, effect_sinks and state_colocation are all unchanged. Only instance_state (7->6) and code_lines (283->280) move the flattering way. A judge scoring the delta would have to decide which figure to believe. I scored the deleted duplication and the fault-site count I measured myself, and I would have reached the same score had every figure moved the other way. WHAT ALMOST STOPPED ME AT 3, twice. (a) The artifact's headline behaviour-preservation evidence is a 3000x60 equivalence run whose script is explicitly NOT in the deliverable (REVISION-NOTES.md:70-71). Scoring rule 1 says score artifacts, never claims, so I gave that paragraph zero weight and supplied the run myself. Anchor 4 says 'shown to be behavior-preserving (D4 >= 3)', and the shipped evidence -- 28 + 37 inherited tests unedited and green, plus a shipped mutation harness whose table is byte-identical -- clears that on its own; my run is corroboration, not the load-bearing beam. A judge who reads anchor 4 as requiring the artifact ITSELF to ship the equivalence evidence should score 3, and that is a defensible reading. (b) The change is small, and 'a simplification' could be read as demanding something structural. I rejected that: the anchor asks for a simplification whose effect was measured, not a large one, and REVISION-NOTES.md:136-192 shows six further candidates considered and each declined with a behavioural reason -- `_committed` kept BECAUSE R2 is the rule that it agrees with the file and deriving it would make R2 true by construction (:138-146); `pop()` declined because it mutates before the rejection test and R4 must stay locally checkable (:160-167). Declining to simplify for a stated behavioural reason is part of 'as simple as its behavior requires, AND NO SIMPLER', which is the dimension's actual question. Prose quality tempted me here more than anywhere and I say so: this is a persuasive document. I gave it a 4 on what I re-ran, not on what it argues.

I note the tension openly: taken literally, anchor 0 ('complexity is unmeasured') is the anchor this packet satisfies -- no descriptor ships with it, mechanical.json arrived empty, and I found no before/after figures anywhere in the read list. I do not score 0 or 1 because anchor 1 requires figures to have been 'measured and reported' and there are none, and because the dimension's own instruction forecloses reading their absence as a defect. What I diffed: I could only diff the two COMPOSITION POINTS, since the flat `../reference/` tree the README compares against is outside my read list -- I did not open it. quota_ledger.py:24-25 and quota_ledger_fake.py:37-38 are the same four lines with one class name changed, over one shared `ReservationBook`; there is no second copy of the rules. Same partition, but the subject component owns nothing and has no internal action, so \"this work belongs to scanners\" restricts nothing by itself. The strongest clause in that brief is the measured SPAN: the action commits lastCommand/result in workflow and complexity_gate in scanners in one step, and the brief says the model asserts those land atomically -- honor it or report the model wrong. * OpenTicket, specs/current under the EMERGENT partition -- REFUSED, and the refusal artifact records verbatim what the vacuous brief would have said (\"component C1, 10 of 10 variables, reaches nothing, zero violations\"), so the failure mode is legible rather than theoretical. * CreateAccount, examples/distributed_history/.../Internal.tla, EMERGENT -- the only FULL brief, and it clears crossing_action_fraction by exactly zero. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE EPIC'S WORKING ASSUMPTIONS, both measured here. (1) AC-01's `consumable_as_architecture` is necessary but NOT sufficient for a non-vacuous brief. It is `partition_source == \"declared\" or decomposes`, which is right for AC-02 -- whose question is whether the project named a boundary to compare code against -- and wrong as AC-03's only gate, because it is true for ANY declared partition including a deliberately useless one. The prompt therefore layers three per-render vacuity tests on top of it: V1 (one component) refuses; V2 (the subject component owns nothing AND has no internal action) and V3 (crossing fraction > 0.5) degrade rather than refuse, because the write-set, effect-port and atomicity clauses are measured PER ACTION and survive a bad partition intact. The two DEGRADED renders above differ by exactly V2, from the same descriptor -- whether a brief constrains anything depends on which component the work lands in, not only on the partition score. (2) \"Neither real model decomposes\" is not what was measured. Internal.tla decomposes EMERGENTLY (2 components, Q = 0.0069, crossing fraction 0.50), and exhaustive search finds decomposing partitions of specs/current itself. A consumer reads that as \"owns nothing\" -- a plausible architectural fact -- when it means \"undefined here\". The text renderer says NOT MEASURABLE; the machine-readable contract that AC-02 and AC-03 actually read does not. Gate A refuses before the field can be reached, which is why the guard is a gate and not a caveat. DOCTRINE. CD-01 holds: neither prompt proposes a cut, a refactor, a target shape or a next step. Move 3's shapes are the vocabulary the measured facts are STATED in -- the brief says \"these are your declared ports\", not \"push effects to the edges\"; \"the model says these commit together\", not \"introduce a commit point\". Both are advisory and gate nothing. The Program Spec Rule is not weakened: the aspect prompt forbids a case module from declaring any state, constant or action, requires EXTENDS over INSTANCE/LOCAL, and keeps the removal test (delete every case module and the program is still fully represented) as the rule rather than a note. WHAT IS NOT SHOWN, and both prompts say so in their own validation sections: nothing here measures whether a brief changes what a coding agent produces. The prompts make the ask derivable and checkable field by field. THE MUTANT MATRIX DID NOT MOVE A SINGLE CELL: ARM A 4/6, ARM B 6/6, guard relaxation 0/3, ordering 0/3, identical to round 1 on both catalogues and on the pytest column, and re-confirmed a third time by a blind agent on a fresh 16-mutant catalogue (0 of 4 guard-accepts on five corpus instruments). Round 1's own conclusion that parameter recovery was part of the reason guard relaxation is unkillable is FALSIFIED, and NEXT-EPIC.md retracts it in place.
THE FINDING OF THE ROUND, which is about the tool this ticket was measuring. Blind run A -- an agent with no epic context, told only to make the architecture report clean -- reported, and the scorer reproduced independently from scratch, that every divergence is erasable with NO declaration edit, no map edit, no blind spot and no basis limit, by re-exporting the offending symbol through a first-party package nested one directory deeper than architecture_reflexion.py's single-path first-party check. Measured: `coherent` on the divergent twin for a 41-line diff, both digests byte-identical to the answer key, blind_spots [], basis_limits [], 8/8 behavioural tests green, and the runtime coupling fully intact. The same defect the other way round flips the COHERENT fixture to `unmappable` when its generated package moves up one directory with zero Python changed -- so this epic's only positive architecture result was conditional on directory depth. EV-03-DF-03, major, FILED NOT FIXED. It is a false clean of exactly the DP-1 class the epic's scoring rule exists to catch, and the rule cannot see it because no declared artifact moved.

Defects 1 and 2 are one fix, because you cannot digest what reaches a judge until you have decided what reaches a judge. 2. A JUDGE WAS SERVED THE FINDING THEY WERE THE INSTRUMENT FOR. Filed as `SM-04-DF-01`; two independent adversarial channels named the right paragraph and the wrong file. 3. D5's ANCHOR IS AMBIGUOUS AND STAYS THAT WAY, VISIBLY. The anchor is untouched. Version 3 does to it what version 2 did to practice: record the choice, never mandate it. It fired once in this round and did exactly what it says -- one judge scored 3 with `anchor_reading: measured` and wrote that under `disclosure` the same lines are a 4. The judge who did NOT reach the field found the sharper thing: the two readings only diverge once anchor 3 holds, so the rule as shipped over-collects, which is the safe direction. 4. `total` IS GONE, and the removal is PRICED rather than assumed. `removal_is_a_delta_rule`: SM-01 seeded for two cuts and neither is this one, so the gap was seeded here, both sides measured in one run. SM-04-GM-T1 -- a dimension score altered in a card, nothing else touched: BEFORE, version 2 card, SEALED:    caught twice (total arithmetic + seal) AFTER,  version 3 card, SEALED:    caught once  (seal digest) -> REDUNDANT BEFORE, version 2 card, UNSEALED:  caught once  (total arithmetic) AFTER,  version 3 card, UNSEALED:  CAUGHT BY NOTHING -> LOAD-BEARING So the cut is free on a sealed card and it is not free on an unsealed one. That is the price and it is in the test, not in prose: `test_the_price_of_removing_total_measured_on_both_sides`. THE RE-SCORE THE CHANGE RULE REQUIRES. Four fresh blind judges, one sealed artifact, two under a frozen version 2 rubric and two under version 3, same day, same dispatch. The bump: 3 points of summed |movement| over 10 judge-scores, worst 1 per judge, all on D4 and D5; D1, D2 and D3 moved zero. FI-03's bump was 4 over 30, worst 1 -- same worst case, higher per-score rate on a quarter of the sample. NOTHING HERE SAYS THE BUMP IS FREE. THE FINDING THE CORE CANNOT EXPRESS, and it is unflattering to version 2's own rationale. FI-03 explained D4 by JUDGING PRACTICE and version 2 was built on that explanation. All four judges here recorded `executed_own_faults: true`, and D4 came out 2, 3, 3, 4 -- with a -2 against FI-03's version 2 row, practice recorded true at BOTH ends. Recording the practice made the variable visible; it did not make the dimension stable. `SM-04-DF-07`. The decontamination is confounded with the round and that half is filed as a HYPOTHESIS, not a cause. AND THE ONE ABOUT D2, WHICH THIS TICKET MAY NOT TOUCH. D2 = 2 on 31 of 31 cards ever written; these four are the 28th to the 31st and the first served a card that told them nothing about how D2 has scored. All four gave anchor 3's unreachability as the reason, unprompted. A judge then found a SECOND crack: read cumulatively, D2 anchor 2 sits above anchor 0's \"complexity is unmeasured\", so an artifact measuring none is forced to 0 -- a 2-to-4-point spread, wider than the D5 one version 3 exists to record. Filed as `SM-04-DF-06` and NOT FIXED. Rewriting D2's anchors would pre-decide SM-05, which is the one thing this ticket was told twice not to do. A SHIPPED TRIPWIRE CAUGHT THIS TICKET AND WAS NOT FIXED BY EXEMPTION. Declaring the version bump as an instrument change made `audit` report nine SUPERSEDED-UNMARKED violations at once -- R-H3 firing on the ticket that shipped the change. All nine were answered from the raw data per the card's own straddle warning: six re-affirmed at `2098d55` (nothing measuring kills or complexity imports `score_tools` or reads the rubric -- the three files that name them do so in a docstring), two re-affirmed and widened, and one SUPERSEDED. That last is FI-03's \"at most one dimension-point per judge\", which was a property of two adjacent rounds rather than of the instrument, and which its own `why` had warned was the flattering half of that ticket's numbers. The change is declared with NO `affects`, applying it to every card, which leaves 22 standing OPENs -- scoping it narrower would have kept the audit quiet by narrowing a true statement, and the dilution cost is reported rather than hidden. MY OWN ROUND-CONDUCT ERROR, DISCLOSED. I read both pass-2 cards while their judges were still writing, mistook an in-progress file for an unfilled one, and messaged two judges mid-score. Both correctly refused to change anything and no score moved. Contacting a judge during scoring is the operator error this card's version 3 is about, and an operator who hides their own is not entitled to report anyone else's. It is in RESULT.md section 0. DENOMINATOR RULE. Scoring rules 8 -> 9: numerator rose, nothing removed. Card top-level fields 15 -> 14: `total` out, `served_digest`, `file_sha256` and `anchor_reading` in.       "narrative": "specs/results/scorecards/score-drives-validation/GOAL-scored-at-goal-time/SV-07/RESULT.md is the evidence ledger; `references/scoring_validation.md` (SV-02) is the design this ticket was sent to implement. WHAT THE TICKET WAS ASKED FOR. SV-02 found one property that separates well-validated from badly-validated code without grading which tools made the tests, priced three carriers for it against the real renderer, and defended the cheapest -- sharpening the recorded-note prompt that already elicits it, at minus fifteen bytes and no new rung. The work order said ship that, and bound it with three constraints: do not restore a retired dimension, do not add a rung, do not force a card bump. WHAT CAME BACK. The prompt is built and prices at exactly the figure SV-02 predicted, and it cannot go into the card at this ticket. A recorded note's prompt is inside BOTH of the card's seals -- the payload `load_rubric` digests, and the bytes `serve` emits, which the version history declares per version. Put the priced prompt in and change nothing else, and the card's own change rule refuses it: bump the card, or restore the text. The card's own version 5 row is the precedent, because it moved no anchor, moved only served bytes, and took a bump to do it. So BOTH carriers cost a version bump, which was the decisive argument SV-02 used against the rung. Filed as SV-07-DF-01 and not fixed, because the work order says a required bump is a finding and not a licence, and because the bump additionally owes the change rule's re-score of a prior example under both versions, which is a judging round and belongs to the evaluation ticket. WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD, at zero bytes on the served surface. `scripts/candidate_note_bar.py` derives the candidate bar from the card at run time, applies exactly one substitution, adds the version row the change rule requires, and prices the result with the real renderer: 6,281 to 6,266 bytes, 9 to 9 rungs, anchors digest byte-identical, exactly one served line moved. What CA-01 measured is what the HARNESS puts in a dispatched agent's context before it reads anything, and no TLA+ variable can see that.
THE MEASUREMENT. Four agents dispatched, asked only to report their own pre-read context verbatim and what they rejected. Three of four received the operator's `MEMORY.md` in full plus the five most recent commit subject lines before any tool call; one (`Explore`) received neither. That CORRECTS `SV-05-DF-02`'s "4 of 4" to a tier and narrows a published figure. The half that survives is the half that matters: it reaches the agent types this project actually uses for judges.
MEASURED ALTERNATIVES, each refused with a reason. (1) Ship `Explore` as the blinding mechanism. Cheapest result available; would
    have closed this ticket with ZERO new apparatus and no `GOAL-apparatus-cut`
    regression. Refused: one observation, one harness version, undocumented
    behaviour, and the `Explore` arm shared the leaking session so cwd does not
    explain it. `SV-05-DF-01` is this project's own precedent for what that bet
    costs -- a version flag that served the wrong card and was accepted.
(2) `claude --bare`. The harness's own switch, documented to skip auto-memory,
    hooks and CLAUDE.md discovery in one flag -- strictly better than what
    shipped. Unusable here: it forces `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper`
    and never reads OAuth or the keychain, and no key is set. `CA-01-DF-02`.
(3) `--safe-mode`. Plausible, keeps normal auth, NOT documented to disable
    auto-memory. Not measured, so nothing is claimed in either direction.

    `*.py`, so shell would have cost zero MEASURED lines for identical
    function. Refused as gaming the denominator; written in Python and priced.

    blocking finding into a clean pass in one settings change. Refused: it is
    the operator's machine, the charter forbids applying such a change, and it
    was never measured to work.

Suite: .../CA-02/pytest-repo-unit.txt and .../CA-02/pytest-repo-unit-reconciled.txt. Spec-unit: .../CA-02/spec-unit-tests.txt. Local signal: .../CA-02/local-signal-apparatus-cut.txt.
WHAT THE MACHINE-CHECKED CORE ABOVE CANNOT EXPRESS.
The complexity delta is zero and the ticket removed 1,444 Python lines, because what was cut was never in the model. `examples/validation/` 15,901 -> 14,457; `scripts/` unchanged at 27,652; `tests/` 32,162 -> 31,274; card unchanged at 6,281 bytes and digest `sha256:2d7d4a0506d9b259`. The surfaces are reported separately and none is added to the card.
WHY THE CUT IS ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN ON AESTHETICS. `RM-05-DF-01` and `CL-02`: for every fault whose killing nodes all lie in a file the removal deletes, `ENTAILED-SURVIVES` follows from `git show` alone and no other verdict is reachable. `CL-02` re-priced the entire sealed history over kill sets and got `priced rows: [], 0 of 10`. `RM-03`'s "first PRICED removal" was WITHDRAWN when its own zero-gap control returned the same verdict. `RM-02` supplies the argument that does not depend on that zero being right: the catalogues are `ab_quota_ledger` fixtures with no version an adopter receives, and that "survives a zero and survives a defective classifier producing one, because it is not a pricing argument."
THE FINDING THE CORE CANNOT CARRY, and it argues against this ticket: `CA-02-DF-04`. The cut deleted the instrument behind DISPROOF 3 -- "the removal-pricing instrument could only ever return zero", 0 of 9 -- and disproof 3 is what justified the cut. The disproof still READS from the sealed record, which is untouched; what is gone is the ability to RE-DERIVE it. An instrument that measures itself useless licenses its own deletion, after which the measurement cannot be checked. The cut is still right, but the load-bearing argument is RM-02's adoption one, not the 0 of 9.
THE ONE SEALED THING THIS CUT MOVED, stated rather than buried. `rm04_removal_pricer` went `UNDERIVABLE:no-effect-surface`, moving the architecture-tag derivation from `17 of 21` to `16 of 21`, refusals 4 -> 5. denominator_rule: the NUMERATOR fell and the DENOMINATOR HELD at 21 -- nothing left the population, the subject is still declared and its sealed cards still read. It is the first downward move of that figure and the first caused by a deletion rather than a declaration; `RD-06-DF-04` predicted the mechanism and was incomplete about the direction. The demonstration was updated per its own stated rule, with all five superseded figures kept.
THE DELIBERATE RED: DELETED WITH ITS SUBJECT, NOT REPAIRED. `test_nothing_in_the_repository_invokes_the_pricer` lived in `tests/test_price_removal.py`, which tests only the pricer. It was never a code failure -- at the base exactly TWO files tripped it and both are prose, `CLOSE-THE-LOOP-EPIC.md` and `NEXT-EPIC.md`. At this branch's HEAD the same filter returns THREE, including this ticket's own tombstone, so had the test been kept it would be red today with MORE hits than before. Suite numerator 7 -> 6, denominator 1566 -> 1532 (-34 tests). Nothing was repaired and nothing is reported as repaired. `RM-05` had already refused the only available fix -- widening the allow-list -- as "editing a target so a result passes"; this ticket refused it too, and refused the tidier variant of keeping a test whose subject no longer exists purely to preserve a red.
MEASURED ALTERNATIVES REFUSED. (1) Cutting `complexity_ledger.py` to make the `scripts/` column non-zero -- no finding behind it. (2) Deleting the three registry rows instead of retiring them -- `FI-04-DF-04` is exactly the class of a capability leaving a registry without a row. (3) Writing a price-table GENERATOR -- a tool for measuring the cutting of apparatus is apparatus, and `RD-02`'s census is the worked example of that becoming a thing a later ticket has to remove; the format is a plain markdown file with no code behind it. (4) Restoring a Python file under `gap_mutants/` to keep the derivation at 17 of 21 -- that is `MF-020`, fitting the tree to an expected output.
METHOD FAILURE, RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. The first full-suite run was discarded: it was killed at 79% under contention with two concurrent CA-01 review suites, AND contaminated by this ticket writing an evidence file into `specs/` while it was in flight -- the same class the epic owner was bitten by at kickoff, committed by the ticket that had been warned about it. Two clean runs replaced it and agree exactly: 6 failed / 1526 passed, same six failures, on the pre-merge tree and again on the reconciled tip.
A FIFTH UNDECLARED INHERITED RED, reported and not filed because the deferment budget of 5 is spent: the spec-unit target `specs/current` fails with `active_ticket 'PA-01' is not present in the desired ticket plan`.       "narrative": "FULL RECORD: specs/results/scorecards/cut-the-apparatus/CA-04/PRICE-TABLE.md (the cut, its price, what the model can no longer express, and what was rejected) and .../descriptor-comparison.md (the before/after basis).
WHAT THIS CLOSE IS. CA-04 removed oracle 4, the mutation kill test, and with it the last hard static gate in this repository. The finding is RM-03-DF-05, which identified this exact cut, declined it because it was a model delta its own ticket forbade, and whose suggested_fix asked for "its own ticket against the CLI model". Removed: the kill_test variable, the RunKillTest action and the KillTestVerdictRequiresBudgets invariant; RunKillTestAdapter and its binding; kill_rate_floor, the mutation_write port and RunKillTest's port row; three kill_mutants.toml catalogues; three spec-unit adapter tests; scripts/run_kill_test.py; tests/test_kill_test.py; and the `run kill-test` subcommand. scripts/ -1,105 lines. The card is untouched at 6,281 bytes.
THE DECREASE IS LICENSED, AND IT WAS NOT LICENSED WHEN THIS CLOSE WAS FIRST ATTEMPTED. The first attempt was REFUSED by this ledger -- "complexity decreased but the validated-refactor basis is UNVERIFIED ... absent evidence is not passing evidence" -- because CA-04 had run no TLC on either side. That refusal was correct and is kept at .../close-refusal.txt. The basis above was then measured rather than argued around: TLC green on both models, the before-model reconstructed from the branch point and verified by sha AND by reproducing the 563,963-state figure the repository had already recorded for it.
WHAT THE MODEL CAN NO LONGER EXPRESS, which is the price and is not softened: nothing validates the representation against the PROGRAM. The model's own comment said kill_test was "the only one of the four [oracles] that validates the representation against the PROGRAM rather than against itself ... none of them can tell a faithful model from a vacuous one. This can." The cost caps have lost their matching value floor; coverage can drift behind the model silently; and compare_reports, the mechanism separating a legitimate simplification from a disguised deletion, is gone -- in a cutting epic. A green tlc_after is therefore WEAKER evidence here than for an ordinary refactor: it certifies the remaining model's self-consistency, which is precisely the property the kill test existed because TLC could not check.
THE MEASUREMENT THAT GOT WORSE, recorded because the flattering version was already written down and had to be withdrawn: the declared bound fell 1,111,320 -> 277,830, and an earlier draft of the price table called that "now under the declared max_state_space_bound for the first time". It is not. `comparable_to_cap` returns None rather than True for an incomplete bound at or under the cap, and the scanner's advisory changed from `state_space_bound` to `state_space_bound_partial`, "INCOMPLETE and CANNOT be compared". The model did not become compliant; it became unmeasurable against the cap. The refinement search above names the move that would repair that.
TWO ORDERED DELETIONS WERE REFUSED, both on the record rather than on taste. kill_test.py could not be deleted whole: five in-repo consumers import its catalogue parser and suppression scanner, including examples/validation/ab/eval/run_controls.py at MODULE SCOPE, which is the driver RD-03 used for the model-derived columns whose zero unique kills is a load-bearing disproof. Measured by parking the file. The oracle-4 half was cut (839 of 1,149 lines) and the 310-line parser/scanner retained; three of those five consumers were found by the reviewer, not by me. candidate_note_bar.py was not deleted at all: SV-06-DF-04 does not say what four documents say it says, "the shortest test asserts nothing imports it" is false (it asserts the card is still 6,281 bytes, the only such assertion in the repository), it is the named reproduction of the open SV-07-DF-01, and instruments.toml declares it with two demonstration nodes. CA-04-DF-01 through -03.
THE MOST TRANSFERABLE RESULT IS CA-04-DF-06 AND IT GENERALISES BEYOND THIS CUT. The epic's REQUIRED loader check greps deleted PATHS, so it is structurally blind to deleted INTERFACES -- CLI subcommands, exported symbols, manifest keys and TOML sections have no basename to grep for. Every cutting ticket in this programme runs a check that cannot see the interfaces it retires, and shipped adopter-facing instructions rot with nothing going red. Demonstrated on this ticket's own cut: SKILL.md:1167 and :1174 still tell adopters to run `tla-spec-dev run kill-test`, which now answers "invalid choice". CA-04-DF-08 is the same defect from the other end -- the validation matrix handed to all eight tickets names `tla-spec-dev run tlc`, and there is no such subcommand.
AND THE FINDING THIS LEDGER PRODUCED ABOUT ITSELF: CA-04-DF-07. A hard gate refused a real promotion, on substance, and it was right. Its decrease clause had been DORMANT for the whole epic -- CA-02 and CA-03 both left validated_refactor entirely at its template default and closed cleanly, because neither changed the model -- and it fired on the first ticket that reached it. Complying with it caught two errors in this ticket's own reporting that nothing else had asked for. The charter carries "static gates catch nothing -- seven epics, zero bugs" among four disproven claims and uses it to forbid adding gates; with CA-03-DF-05's record-checks and CA-05's registry tripwire, that sentence is in serious trouble. This is not a licence to add a gate, and CA-04 added none -- it removed the last hard one.
Eight findings filed against a declared budget of five, all disposed; the overrun is recorded as an overrun. Suite 8 failed / 1466 passed on the merged tip: six pre-existing at CA-03's tip and two this ticket's, both declared, both outside its scope, none repaired.",

THE HONEST NEGATIVE: the reconstructed 12-mutant catalog is identical before and after -- guard relaxation still 0 of 3 by corpus, 3 of 3 by hand-written tests -- because all 330 recovered arguments are arguments the guard ACCEPTS and 0 are rejected inputs (220 refusable pairs exist that a state graph can never emit). Removing the leakage half of EV-02's two causes moves nothing, so the whole remaining failure is the structural half. Separately, the wrong-item class seeded_faults.toml declined to seed as unmeasurable is killed on BOTH instruments; that caveat was a prediction never run and is amended in place.
